title: How universities can lead the way towards a sustainable future
desc:
Join the launch of our Sustainable Imperial Strategy (2026–2031) .

As a community of thinkers, teachers, professionals and innovators – how do we best translat e our sustainability ideas into real work i mpact? How do we bring our ingenuity to guide our institution and the world beyond to a more sustainable future?

Whether you are deeply involved in sustainability or just starting out, you are a vital part of our collective journey towards a more sustainable Imperial and planet.

Across a short presentation, an exhibition showcase, and networking afternoon tea, you’ll meet the staff, students, alumni and community members bringing our sustainability ambitions to reality – and learn how you can get involved.

Join us as we unveil our vision for the next five years and beyond.

title: Weird Weather: The Response by David Shukman
desc:
Join David Shukman, former BBC Science Editor, and Theodore Keeping, wildfire & climate scientist at World Weather Attribution, Imperial College London, for a conversation around how climate change is reshaping our world through increasingly erratic and extreme weather, and how we can respond.

​David’s latest book, The Response: A Story of Fire and Flood in Britain’s New World of Extremes , is a gripping account of the new extremes that our bodies, buildings and landscapes now face in Britain and around the world, compiled through extensive interviews with experts, including researchers from Imperial. The discussion will explore themes from the book, notably wildfires, and the role of communication in driving climate action.

David will also be signing books after the talks. Please note…

title: HEP seminar: Tobias Fitschen (University of Manchester) – Trigger level analysis at ATLAS
desc: The ATLAS Collaboration recently released its full Run-2 dijet Trigger-Level Analysis (TLA), which processes an unprecedented dataset of more than 60 billion events within a single analysis. By reconstructing jets directly in the high-level trigger, TLA achieves a data-taking rate more than twenty times higher than the nominal ATLAS readout. This approach enables searches for new physics in dijet final states that would otherwise be limited by data-acquisition bandwidth. While conventional LHC dijet searches are typically restricted to masses above 1 TeV, the presented analysis extends the accessible mass range down to 375 GeV. As a result, the presented analysis sets world-leading exclusion limits for simplified dark matter models.

title: Junior Geometry Seminar – Nick Manrique
desc:
Title: Regularisations of the area functional

Speaker: Nick Manrique

Abstract: The problem of finding minimal surfaces in general manifolds has been of significant interest to differential geometers for at least 100 years. In broad terms, this can be construed as the problem of finding critical points of the area functional defined on some appropriate space of surfaces. Making sense of this is not easy, for one because it is not clear what the appropriate space should be. All available options come with significant technical challenges.

In the 1970s, the school of de Giorgi proposed a different approach whereby the area functional is ‘regularised’ to a family of functionals depending on some small parameter. This family has the benefit of being defined on a standard function space and…

desc:
This event is open to staff and students across Imperial College London.

Synthetic biology is poised to be one of the defining technologies of our time with the potential to transform how we treat disease, monitor our environments, and manufacture chemicals. title: In-person session – Bloating workshop
desc: Join us for an intimate, evidence-based workshop exploring one of the most common digestive symptoms experienced by adults in the UK: bloating. In this small-group session, we’ll take a deep dive into gut health, exploring the many possible causes of bloating and why symptoms can vary so widely from person to person. You’ll learn how to better identify your own symptom patterns, understand potential triggers, and gain practical insight into what your body may be telling you. The session will include a 20-minute evidence-based Gut-Directed Hypnosis session designed specifically to support bloating management.
